stories.h: Trump says US may have to give Iran 'the hammer', Tehran warns of long war
stories.p: US President Donald Trump has reportedly told a rally in Iowa that America may eventually have to strike Iran again, saying he has held back to save lives. Iran's army says any new war would last longer than before.
body: US President Donald Trump has renewed his threats of further military action against Iran, and Tehran has warned that any new war would be longer and wider than past hostilities.
## What Trump said

Speaking at a rally in Iowa on Sunday, 1 November 2026, ahead of the US midterm elections on 3 November, Trump reportedly said the only reason he had not finished with Iran was that he wanted to be nice and save lives, but that at some point the US would have to give Iran 'the hammer'. The comments followed earlier signals from his administration that more targets were being considered.
## Iran's response

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said on state television that Iran was fully prepared for a long conflict. He warned that a future war could last longer than previous fighting and that the American president would not be able to decide when or how it would end.
## Background

Tensions between the two countries have remained high since earlier US strikes on Iran. Iran's Supreme Leader warned the US and Israel last week against new attacks. Trump has made his tough stance on Iran part of his campaign message ahead of the midterm elections, in which control of Congress is at stake.
## Why it matters
Any new conflict in the region could push up global oil prices, which affects Nigeria's earnings from crude oil as well as fuel prices around the world.
more: Trump told an Iowa rally the US may have to give Iran 'the hammer'.
Iran says it is ready for a long war.
The US midterm elections take place on 3 November.

stories.h: Rufai Oseni says law letting states run their own electricity will never work
stories.p: Broadcaster Rufai Oseni has reportedly said states lack the money, gas and grid to generate their own power, arguing that the government should fix the national grid instead.
body: Television presenter Rufai Oseni has dismissed the law that allows Nigeria's states to generate and distribute their own electricity, saying it cannot work in practice.
## What he said

Speaking on a breakfast television programme on Monday, 2 November 2026, Oseni reportedly said the idea of decentralising power sounds good in theory, but most states lack the money, technical skill and infrastructure to carry it out. He said the power sector needs huge investment, steady gas supply, power plants, transmission lines and working distribution networks, and asked how many states could provide these.
## His argument

Oseni noted that the federal government, after running the sector for more than four decades, still struggles to supply a steady 4,000 to 5,000 megawatts to a population of over 200 million, and that the national grid often collapses. He added that many states struggle to pay civil servants and depend on monthly federal allocations, so they cannot be expected to fund power plants costing billions of dollars. He questioned how the country could split supply into 36 centres when it could not provide 24-hour power from one, and urged the government to focus on fixing the grid and gas supply.
## Background

The Electricity Act of 2023 allows states to regulate and develop their own electricity markets, and several states, including Lagos, Enugu and Ondo, have set up their own regulators. Supporters of the law say it will attract investment and bring power closer to consumers. Electricity has also become a campaign issue, with opposition candidate Atiku Abubakar accusing President Tinubu of failing to keep his power promises, while the government points to its grid expansion plans.
more: Oseni says most states lack the money, gas and grid.
He says the federal government still struggles with 4,000–5,000MW.
He urged a focus on fixing the national grid.

stories.h: Governor Alex Otti opens Abia State facilities to opposition parties, says politics should not deny anyone access
stories.p: Abia State Governor Alex Otti says opposition parties should be allowed to use government-owned facilities in the state, including the stadium, as long as they follow due process and pay the required fees. He says he has already directed that no party be turned away because it is in opposition.
body: Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has made it clear that opposition political parties should be allowed to use government-owned facilities in the state, provided they follow the proper procedures and pay the required fees.
## The directive

According to the governor, he has already given instructions that no political party should be prevented from using public facilities, including the stadium, simply because it belongs to the opposition.
## A message of political tolerance

Otti's position sends an important message about tolerance and fairness. Government facilities are maintained with public resources, and access to them should not depend on which party someone supports.

This is one area where Nigerian politicians need to learn to separate governance from party politics. You can disagree with your opponents and campaign against them, and still respect their right to operate within the law.
Governor Otti appears to be making that distinction clear in Abia State.
## The big question
How many Nigerian governors would willingly allow opposition parties to use government facilities for their political activities?
Politics should never be an excuse to deny citizens their rights.
more: Opposition parties can use Abia facilities, including the stadium.
They must follow due process and pay the required fees.
Otti says he has already given the directive.

stories.h: Nine killed as Bahamas-bound private jet plunges into Florida roadside
stories.p: A Learjet 60 carrying nine people crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday, killing everyone on board. The pilot had reported ice and turbulence before declaring an emergency, and the jet narrowly missed homes and a busy road.
body: A private jet carrying nine people crashed beside a road in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday, 1 November 2026, killing everyone on board in a fireball that was caught on video by passing motorists.
## What happened

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the Learjet 60 went down at about 12.50pm local time and described the crash as a horrific tragedy. The aircraft had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was flying to the Bahamas. Florida governor Ron DeSantis said there were no immediate reports of anyone on the ground being hurt, and described the crash as cataclysmic, saying the plane looked like a missile coming down and left a large crater by the roadside. Reports said the site was a few miles from President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate.
## The final minutes

According to air traffic control recordings and flight tracking data, the jet was cruising at about 35,000 feet when the pilots reported light ice, moderate turbulence and rain, and asked to climb a further 2,000 feet. Shortly afterwards the plane went into a steep dive. The pilot declared a mayday, reporting that the aircraft was descending at 10,000 and then 20,000 feet per minute in an overspeed condition, before saying the jet was going to crash. Tracking data showed the rate of descent at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.
## The investigation

The National Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation, supported by a team from the Federal Aviation Administration. The airport confirmed it was a private flight but did not say who was on board. Records list the plane's owner as a company registered in Delaware. Heavy rain had hit the region on Sunday, and a flood watch was in place until Monday afternoon.
## Co-pilot identified

On Monday, relatives identified the co-pilot as 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha, who grew up in Palm Beach County. She earned her private pilot's licence at 17, in October 2023, before she could even drive, and had trained at a flight school with a branch in Pompano Beach. She had said she dreamed of becoming a commercial airline pilot. The other victims have not yet been publicly named.
## Victims named

On Monday, relatives identified the passengers as a 44-year-old technology entrepreneur, his wife and their two children, aged two and four, together with two close friends of the family and the children's nanny. The two pilots, an experienced aviator and his 20-year-old co-pilot, also died. In a statement, the families thanked first responders and the Palm Beach County community and said their hearts were also with the pilots' families.
## What happens next
Investigators are expected to examine the wreckage, the weather and the aircraft's maintenance history.
more: All nine people on board the Learjet 60 were killed.
The pilot reported ice and turbulence before a steep dive.
The co-pilot was a 20-year-old from Palm Beach County.

stories.h: Peller apologises after calling himself Jesus Christ on livestream
stories.p: Streamer Peller has apologised after a livestream clip showed him in a white costume asking a guest to call him Jesus Christ. The guest objected on camera, and many viewers said his apology did not go far enough.
body: Popular streamer Habeeb Adelaja, known as Peller, has apologised after a clip from his livestream in which he referred to himself as Jesus Christ drew widespread criticism.
## What happened

In the clip, which spread online on Sunday, 1 November 2026, Peller appeared in a white and red costume with a wig and greeted his guest as Jesus Christ. The guest refused to go along with the joke and told him not to disrespect any religion, pointing out that someone with about 17 million followers had a responsibility to the people watching. Peller argued that he was only wearing a costume and that nobody alive knows what Jesus looked like. During the exchange he also said he was a traditionalist and joked about dressing as an Imam the next day, which the people with him warned was only making things worse.
## The apology

In a follow-up video posted the same day, Peller said he had not expected the outfit to cause such a reaction, describing it as just a white cloth. He described himself as both a Christian and a Muslim, apparently to show that he meant no offence to either faith, and asked his fans to forgive him.
## How people reacted

Many social media users criticised the stunt, saying religion should not be used for content. Some said the apology fell short because he did not clearly admit he was wrong, while others defended him as a young entertainer who made a mistake.
## Background

Peller, one of Nigeria's best-known TikTok streamers, is often in the news for his livestreams. Last week, rapper YCee used his name as an example of what he called brain-rot content and refused to apologise for it. Peller and fellow content creator Jarvis held a white wedding in Lekki, Lagos, in August.
more: His guest objected on camera and refused to play along.
Peller said he did not expect the costume to offend anyone.

stories.h: Toluwanising burial row resolved as widow and father agree, Woli Arole calls for calm
stories.p: A close associate of the late gospel singer Toluwanising says his widow and father have agreed to bury him at his Ibadan house, ending their dispute. Comedian-turned-pastor Woli Arole has urged people to stop using the singer's death for online attention.
body: The dispute over where gospel singer Toluwanising should be buried appears to have been settled, according to one of his closest colleagues.
## The agreement

In an Instagram video shared on Sunday, 1 November 2026, singer Lanre Alewilese said the widow, Damilola Olayemi, and her father-in-law had agreed that the singer should be buried at his house in Ibadan, Oyo State. He described the disagreement as a misunderstanding and asked Nigerians to let the family settle the matter in peace. He also appealed to people to stop attacking the widow, describing her as a young woman going through a very difficult time, and said members of the singer's band could vouch for her character.
## Woli Arole speaks

On Monday, 2 November, comedian-turned-pastor Bayegun Oluwatoyin, known as Woli Arole, posted a video in which he condemned people seeking social media attention from the tragedy. Quoting Proverbs 31:8 on speaking up for those who cannot speak for themselves, he described Toluwanising as a rare talent, and questioned why some of those now talking about him had shown little interest in his music while he was alive. He urged the public to support the widow and children, and said no dispute could take away the music the singer left behind. His comments came after unproven claims made online by a preacher based in Canada named him and other gospel figures in connection with the death.
## Background

Toluwanising, 32, died suddenly on 14 October 2026, and a night of tributes was held for him in Ibadan on 27 October. His father had insisted that he be buried at the family residence or in his hometown near his late mother, and relatives had claimed that the widow preferred a cemetery. His younger brother later defended the widow, as did media personality Nancy Umeh.
## What happens next
A burial date has not yet been announced.
more: Lanre Alewilese says the widow and father have agreed on a burial at his house.
Woli Arole urged people to stop using the death for clout.

stories.h: Don Jazzy says he blew his first big music money on 50 bottles of champagne
stories.p: Mavin Records boss Don Jazzy says he spent his first big earnings from music on champagne and clubbing before he started investing in new artistes. He says that decision means he no longer has to work, and urged young people to invest early.
body: Music producer and Mavin Records founder Michael Collins Ajereh, better known as Don Jazzy, has admitted that he wasted his first major earnings from music, and says the lesson changed his life.
## What he said

Speaking on an episode of the 'On The Grind' podcast, in comments that spread on Monday, 2 November 2026, Don Jazzy said that when he got his first big money from music, he bought 50 bottles of champagne and went clubbing. He said he quickly pulled himself together and began investing in signing new artistes, adding that, as a result, he no longer has to work.
## His advice

The producer urged young people to put the money they earn in their youth into profitable businesses rather than spending it on luxuries. He said they did not necessarily need to start a record label, but should find something lucrative to invest in.
## Background

Don Jazzy co-founded Mo' Hits Records with D'banj in 2004 and produced many of the label's biggest hits. After the label split in 2012, he set up Mavin Records, which has gone on to sign and develop stars such as Tiwa Savage, Rema, Ayra Starr, Johnny Drille and Crayon. The label attracted a major investment from Universal Music Group in 2024. He is also known for his generosity online and recently announced a technology scholarship for young Nigerians.
## How people reacted

Many social media users praised his honesty and said the advice was useful for young people who start earning early. Others joked that 50 bottles of champagne would be a dream night out, while some pointed out that his success depended on spotting talent, which not every investor can do.
more: Don Jazzy says he bought 50 bottles of champagne with his first big money.
He then invested in signing new artistes.

stories.h: Ebonyi governor sends bill to make kidnapping punishable by death
stories.p: Ebonyi governor Francis Nwifuru says he has sent a bill to the state House of Assembly to make kidnapping punishable by death by hanging. He announced it at the funeral of a monarch who was abducted and killed in March.
body: Ebonyi State governor Francis Nwifuru says he has sent a bill to the state House of Assembly that would make kidnapping punishable by death by hanging, with no other option.
## Where he said it

Nwifuru made the announcement over the weekend at the funeral of HRH Eze Francis Igwe, the traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike autonomous community in Ikwo Local Government Area. The monarch, the father of a former deputy governor of the state, Eric Igwe, was abducted on Sunday, 1 March 2026, while travelling to church, and was reportedly killed by his captors the next day.
## What he said

The governor said the bill was meant to deter anyone planning a kidnapping, whether for money or for political reasons. He said he would not delay in carrying out any court judgment against those arrested over the monarch's killing, and that the murder must be the last of its kind in Ikwo and across the state. He also expressed concern about what he described as a moral decline among young people and urged them to turn away from crime.
## Tributes

Former governors Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi and former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim paid tribute to the late monarch, describing him as a peacemaker, educationist and good administrator who brought projects such as the Folk Technical College to his community. His eldest son said his father's last wish was for Governor Nwifuru to win a second term.
## Background

Several Nigerian states already have laws that allow the death penalty for kidnapping, but executions are rare because governors must sign death warrants. Human rights groups oppose the death penalty, while supporters argue it is needed to deter a crime that has spread across the country.
## What happens next
The bill must be passed by the House of Assembly and signed by the governor before it becomes law.
more: The bill would make kidnapping punishable by death by hanging.
He announced it at the funeral of a monarch killed by kidnappers.
The Assembly must pass the bill before it becomes law.

stories.h: Two suspected Ebola cases in Adamawa test negative, NCDC says
stories.p: The NCDC says two people isolated in Yola, Adamawa State, with suspected Ebola tested negative after two rounds of tests. The earlier case in the FCT remains Nigeria's only confirmed case.
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) says two people investigated for suspected Ebola virus disease in Adamawa State have tested negative.
## What happened

NCDC Director-General Jide Idris said the Adamawa State Public Health Emergency Operations Centre received a report in the early hours of 30 October 2026 after two people in Yola developed symptoms that needed further investigation. The two were isolated, public health measures were started and samples were collected. Idris said the samples came back negative for Ebola after two rounds of testing.
## Nigeria's only case

Idris said the case confirmed earlier in the Federal Capital Territory remained the only laboratory-confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria. That patient had recently travelled to Uganda and was later evacuated to Switzerland for treatment, while dozens of contacts were monitored. He praised the Adamawa Commissioner for Health and the state response team for acting quickly, and said the NCDC would keep supporting the state.
## Contacts being monitored

In its latest situation report, published on Monday, 2 November, the NCDC said 62 contacts of the confirmed case had been identified and are being followed up. Their monitoring periods end on different dates between 31 October and 13 November 2026, so 13 November is the latest date on which follow-up of the current contacts is expected to finish. The agency said it had trained more contact tracers and that surveillance continues.
## Advice to the public

The NCDC urged people to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified claims and rely on official channels for updates. Anyone with fever, severe weakness, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding, especially after possible exposure, should seek medical help immediately, tell health workers about any travel or contact with sick people, and avoid self-medication.
## Background

The current outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, began in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May and has recorded more than 10,000 confirmed cases and close to 5,000 deaths, mostly in the DR Congo. Africa CDC has warned that the continent is not winning the fight, and African health ministers have agreed to strengthen border surveillance.
more: Both samples tested negative after two rounds.
The FCT case remains Nigeria's only confirmed case.
Monitoring of 62 contacts is due to end by 13 November.

stories.h: Some households report ₦25,000 alerts under government's HoPE cash transfer
stories.p: Some vulnerable households have reportedly received ₦25,000 payment alerts under the federal government's HoPE cash transfer programme, which is meant to pay ₦75,000 over three months. The government has not confirmed how widely payments have gone out.
body: Some poor households have reportedly started receiving payments under the federal government's Household Prosperity and Empowerment (HoPE) Cash Transfer Programme, according to reports at the weekend.
## What has been reported

Several beneficiaries said they received text messages showing that ₦25,000 had been paid into their accounts through microfinance banks and payment providers. Under the programme, eligible households are expected to receive ₦25,000 a month for three months, a total of ₦75,000 per household. The money is meant to help families with food, transport and other basic needs.
## What is not yet clear

The government has not confirmed how many households have been paid or whether payments have started nationwide. Reports say payment dates may differ from one beneficiary to another, and that not every eligible household will be paid at the same time.
## Beware of scams

Beneficiaries are being advised to confirm any payment alert with their bank or payment provider through official customer service channels, and not to share passwords, PINs or other private details with anyone. People are also warned to ignore offers of registration for a fee, as the programme does not charge people to enrol.
## Background

The government has run several cash transfer schemes since the removal of the petrol subsidy in 2023, aimed at cushioning the effect of rising prices on the poorest households. A separate scheme offering ₦50,000 a month to some vulnerable Nigerians was announced recently. Critics have questioned how beneficiaries are selected and whether payments reach the right people, while the government says it uses the national social register.
## What it means
For families who receive the money, the payments offer some relief, but many Nigerians say the amounts are small compared with the cost of living.
more: Eligible households are to get ₦25,000 a month for three months.
The government has not confirmed nationwide payments.
Beneficiaries are warned against scams.

stories.h: Bauchi local government chairman dies in road crash three months after election
stories.p: Masud Aliyu Umar, chairman of Zaki Local Government Area in Bauchi State, has died in a road accident in Darazo LGA, less than three months after he was elected. Governor Bala Mohammed called his death a devastating loss.
body: The chairman of Zaki Local Government Area in Bauchi State, Masud Aliyu Umar, has died in a road accident, barely three months after he took office.
## What happened

The crash happened on the evening of Sunday, 1 November 2026, at Konkiyal village in Darazo Local Government Area, according to reports. Umar was returning to Zaki after attending a stakeholders' meeting of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Bauchi, the state capital. Details of how the accident happened and whether anyone else was hurt have not been made public.
## Who he was

Umar was elected chairman on 17 August 2026, along with the chairmen of the other 19 local government areas in the state. Before that, he served as director-general of the Bauchi State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), where he was credited with leading the state's disaster response and humanitarian work.
## Governor's tribute

Governor Bala Mohammed described the death as a devastating loss to the state. In a statement issued through his media aide, Mukhtar Gidado, he described Umar as a dedicated public servant, a committed grassroots politician and a compassionate leader. He said that despite his short time as chairman, Umar had shown strong commitment to empowering young people and women and to development in Zaki. The governor sent condolences to the family, the people of Zaki, the Katagum Emirate Council and the state chapter of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria.
## Funeral
The governor said funeral prayers would be held on Monday, 2 November, at 2pm at the palace of the District Head of Mur Mur in Zaki Local Government Area.
## Background
Road accidents remain one of the leading causes of death in Nigeria, and many involve officials travelling at night on poor roads.
more: Umar died in a crash at Konkiyal village in Darazo LGA.

stories.h: Broda Mike says Ghe Ghe's sister's online attack was planned, replying to VeryDarkMan
stories.p: Skit maker Broda Mike has claimed that he and Ghe Ghe planned for Ghe Ghe's sister to criticise him online, in a reply to VeryDarkMan. Many users said this suggests the drama was staged for content.
body: Skit maker Broda Mike has made a surprising claim in his reply to social media activist VeryDarkMan (VDM), saying a recent online family drama involving internet personality Ghe Ghe was planned.
## What he said

VDM had reportedly claimed that he helped Ghe Ghe when Ghe Ghe's sister publicly criticised him online. Responding in a video shared on Monday, 2 November 2026, Broda Mike said that he and Ghe Ghe had planned for the sister to drag Ghe Ghe on social media. He did not explain why, or whether the sister knew it was staged.
## How people reacted

The claim drew mixed reactions. Many users said it confirmed their suspicion that much online drama is staged for content, and some said they felt deceived. One user noted that Ghe Ghe's sister had gone further than any plan by publicly claiming she had not received ₦5 million. Others mocked everyone involved. Ghe Ghe and his sister have not publicly responded to Broda Mike's claim.
## Background

VDM has been in several online disputes in recent weeks, including with Davido's camp, Zlatan Ibile, former BBNaija winner Phyna and businessman Blord. He has also been promoting his Ratel brand of power products, which he says sold ₦90 million worth in one day. Content creators have increasingly been accused of staging arguments and family disputes to attract views, and the latest claim is likely to add to that debate.
## What happens next
It is not yet clear whether VDM will respond, but fans expect the exchange to continue online.
more: Broda Mike says he and Ghe Ghe planned the sister's attack.
Many users said the drama was staged for content.

stories.h: Eedris Abdulkareem denies joining APC, hits back at Isaac Fayose
stories.p: Veteran rapper Eedris Abdulkareem has denied claims attributed to Isaac Fayose that he has joined the APC, calling Fayose a hypocrite. The exchange has drawn amused reactions online.
body: Veteran rapper Eedris Abdulkareem has rejected a claim that he has joined the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), and aimed a sharp reply at Isaac Fayose, the younger brother of former Ekiti governor Ayodele Fayose.
## What he said

In a post shared on Monday, 2 November 2026, Eedris dismissed the claim, which was reportedly made by Isaac Fayose, calling him an 'agbaya', a Yoruba word for an older person who behaves badly, and saying his new name was hypocrisy. He did not set out his current political position in the post.
## Background

Eedris, best known for the 2004 hit 'Jaga Jaga', has long been a critic of Nigerian governments and political leaders, including President Bola Tinubu. In 2025 he released a song criticising the government, which the broadcasting regulator restricted on air. Isaac Fayose is an outspoken political commentator who often comments on national issues online. His brother, Ayodele Fayose, is a member of the PDP but has openly backed President Tinubu's re-election.
## How people reacted

Many social media users were amused by the exchange, with some saying they were waiting to see how Isaac Fayose would respond. Others criticised Isaac Fayose, while some said they were glad Eedris had not changed his political stance.
## What happens next
Isaac Fayose has not yet responded publicly. Political arguments among celebrities are expected to grow as campaigning for the January 2027 elections heats up.
more: Eedris says he has not joined the APC.
He called Isaac Fayose a hypocrite.
Isaac Fayose has not yet responded.

stories.h: Politics will shock you: Soludo's son seen promoting NDC song while his father backs Tinubu
stories.p: A Facebook video reportedly showing Ozonna Soludo, son of Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo, dancing to and promoting a song associated with the NDC has sparked reactions online. The NDC is linked in online discussions to Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, while Governor Soludo has reportedly been mobilising support for President Bola Tinubu.
body: Nigerian politics has taken another interesting turn, and this time the attention is on the family of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Charles Soludo.
## The video

A Facebook video reportedly showing Ozonna Soludo, the governor's son, dancing to and promoting a song associated with the NDC has sparked reactions online. In online discussions, the NDC has been linked to Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso.
## Father and son in different camps?
What makes the situation interesting is the apparent political contrast between father and son.

While Ozonna appears to be enjoying a song associated with a different political camp, his father, Governor Soludo, has reportedly been mobilising political stakeholders in Anambra State in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.
## A dance is not a declaration
Dancing to a political song does not automatically mean someone has joined or endorsed a party. Ozonna has not made any confirmed political declaration through the video.

Even so, the moment has attracted attention because of his father's position. It is also a reminder that family ties do not necessarily decide political loyalty. A father may support one candidate while his son prefers another.
## The big question
If Governor Soludo is backing Tinubu while his son appears to be promoting a song associated with Obi and Kwankwaso, what does that say about the changing political atmosphere ahead of 2027?
Politics in Nigeria never stops surprising us.
more: Ozonna Soludo was seen dancing to an NDC-associated song.
Governor Soludo is reportedly mobilising support for Tinubu.
Ozonna has made no confirmed political declaration.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Venezuela to reach U-17 Women's World Cup semi-finals, face Brazil next
stories.p: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Venezuela 1-0 in Morocco through a late penalty from captain Azeezat Oduntan to reach the semi-finals of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. They are Africa's last team in the tournament and will play Brazil on Wednesday.
body: Nigeria's under-17 women's team, the Flamingos, are into the semi-finals of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco.
## The match

The Flamingos beat Venezuela 1-0 in the quarter-final on Sunday, 1 November 2026, at the Mohammed VI Football Academy in Salé. Captain Azeezat Oduntan scored the winner from the penalty spot in the 89th minute after Oluebube Umejiaku was fouled in the box, a decision confirmed by a VAR review.
## What comes next

Nigeria will face Brazil in the semi-final on Wednesday, 4 November, at the Moulay El Hassan Stadium in Rabat. They are the only African side left in the competition after Ghana lost 1-0 to Japan in their quarter-final.
## Reactions

The Confederation of African Football congratulated the team on social media, celebrating their place in the last four. Nigerian fans also shared videos of the players dancing and celebrating after earlier victories in the tournament.
## Background

Nigeria has a strong record in women's youth football and has reached the later stages of age-group World Cups several times. The senior team, the Super Falcons, are the most successful side in African women's football and won another Women's Africa Cup of Nations title this year. The Flamingos' run has raised hopes of Nigeria's first-ever U-17 women's world title.
more: Azeezat Oduntan scored an 89th-minute penalty.
Nigeria play Brazil in the semi-final on Wednesday in Rabat.
They are Africa's last team in the tournament.

stories.h: Dangote cuts petrol gantry price again, now ₦1,210 per litre
stories.p: The Dangote Refinery has reportedly reduced its petrol gantry price by ₦55 to ₦1,210 per litre, citing a fall in European petrol benchmark prices. Depot prices in Lagos have also dropped, averaging about ₦1,259 per litre.
body: Petrol prices are falling again in Nigeria after the Dangote Refinery announced another cut.
## The new price

According to reports on Monday, 2 November 2026, the refinery reduced its petrol gantry price by ₦55, from ₦1,265 to ₦1,210 per litre, a drop of about 4.35 per cent. The cut was announced through marketers linked to the refinery. Industry sources said it followed a fall in the European petrol benchmark that the refinery uses to set its prices, as well as better supply.
## Depot prices

Other Lagos depots had already reduced their prices at the end of last week. Depot owners including African Terminal, Rainoil, Ardova and NIPCO were selling petrol at about ₦1,260 per litre, with Aiteo slightly lower at ₦1,255. Prices also fell in Port Harcourt and Calabar. Diesel prices have moved in the opposite direction after the refinery raised its diesel gantry price last week.
## What it means for motorists

Gantry and depot prices are what marketers pay before selling at filling stations, so the cuts could lead to lower pump prices in the coming days. However, actual pump prices also depend on transport costs and how quickly retailers pass on savings.
## Background

This is the refinery's second petrol price cut in less than a week. Since fuel subsidies were removed in 2023, prices have been set by the market, and the Dangote Refinery has become a major influence on what Nigerians pay at the pump.
more: Dangote's gantry price falls by ₦55 to ₦1,210 per litre.
The cut follows lower European petrol prices.

stories.h: Davido says he would charge $500,000 a show for a joint tour with Wizkid
stories.p: Davido has reportedly said a joint tour with Wizkid would sell out every venue and that he would charge $500,000 per show. He also explained why the two have not recorded a song together in about 10 years.
body: Davido has once again got fans talking about a possible joint tour with his long-time rival, Wizkid.
## What he said

In an interview on the IONWANNATALK show, clips of which spread online on 1 and 2 November 2026, Davido reportedly said that if he and Wizkid toured together, he would ask for $500,000 per show because every venue would sell out. He was less sure that a joint song would be a hit, pointing to past collaborations between big stars that he said did not do as well as expected.
## On the rivalry

Davido said the two had not recorded together in about 10 years, not because they could not work together, but because they were not in the same mental space. He acknowledged that people have different views on whether the rivalry helped or hurt their careers, and said he had once felt strongly about their differences but no longer did.
## Background

Davido and Wizkid are two of the biggest names in Afrobeats. They collaborated in the early 2010s, but fans have long been divided into rival camps, and the two have occasionally traded words online. Davido has been in the news this week over his breakdown in relations with VeryDarkMan and his support for Zlatan's song 'Inferno'.
## How fans reacted
Fans were excited by the idea of a joint tour, with many saying it would be the biggest event in African music. Wizkid had not responded at the time of the report.
more: Davido says a joint tour would sell out every venue.
He would charge $500,000 per show.
He and Wizkid have not recorded together in about 10 years.

stories.h: Former Labour Party chairman Abure rules out backing Obi, open to Tinubu or Atiku
stories.p: Julius Abure, the former national chairman of the Labour Party, has reportedly said he will not support Peter Obi in 2027 but could back either President Tinubu or Atiku Abubakar. Obi's camp says it has moved on.
body: Julius Abure, who led the Labour Party when Peter Obi was its presidential candidate in 2023, has said he will not support Obi in the 2027 election.
## What he said

In a newspaper interview reported on Monday, 2 November 2026, Abure reportedly said he was open to working with any of the major candidates but was very sure he would not back Obi, who is now the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate. He said he could support either President Bola Tinubu or Atiku Abubakar of the ADC, depending on the outcome of a pending Supreme Court case on the Labour Party's leadership, whether a candidate's agenda matches his views, and how acceptable the candidate is to voters. He said that if the court has not ruled by the end of November, he will consult his supporters.
## His criticism of Obi

Abure argued that Obi had squandered the goodwill and structures that helped him win more than six million votes in 2023, and predicted he would do worse in 2027. He also questioned Obi's leadership, accusing him and Abia Governor Alex Otti of undermining the party.
## The other side

Obi's allies have previously accused Abure of breaking an agreement to hold an inclusive party convention. The NDC and Obi's camp dismissed his latest comments, saying they have moved on and are focused on the election.
## Background
The Labour Party has been split by a long leadership dispute since the 2023 election, which eventually led Obi to leave and join the NDC.
more: Abure says he will not support Obi.
He could back Tinubu or Atiku depending on a court case.

stories.h: Goodluck and Patience Jonathan among guests at singer L.A.X's Lagos wedding
stories.p: Former President Goodluck Jonathan and his wife Patience were among high-profile guests at singer L.A.X's wedding reception in Lagos, hosted by his father, SIFAX Group chairman Taiwo Afolabi. The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, also attended.
body: Singer L.A.X's wedding celebration in Lagos turned into a gathering of political, royal and entertainment heavyweights.
## The wedding

The singer, whose real name is Damilola Afolabi, held his wedding reception on Victoria Island on Sunday, 1 November 2026. It was hosted by his father, Taiwo Afolabi, chairman of the SIFAX Group. The couple had earlier held a civil ceremony in Malta in September and an Islamic wedding ceremony on 29 October.
## The guests

Former President Goodluck Jonathan and his wife, Patience Jonathan, were among the guests, along with the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, several traditional rulers and stars from the entertainment industry. Lagos monarch Oba Saheed Elegushi and his wife were also pictured at the event.
## How people reacted

Photos and videos of the former First Lady drew warm and nostalgic reactions online. Many users recalled her time in office with affection, while others remembered the viral moments from her public appearances. Fans also congratulated L.A.X on his marriage and remarked on the high-profile guest list.
## Background
L.A.X rose to fame in the mid-2010s with hits such as 'Caro' with Wizkid. His father, Taiwo Afolabi, is a prominent businessman in the maritime sector and a well-known figure in Nigerian society.
more: The reception was hosted by SIFAX chairman Taiwo Afolabi.
The Jonathans and the Emir of Kano attended.

stories.h: Groom reportedly walks out of wedding in Imo State after bride's family demands ₦1.2 million bride price
stories.p: A groom in Mbaise, Imo State, has reportedly walked away from his traditional wedding after the bride's family allegedly demanded ₦1.2 million as bride price. The incident has reopened debate about the cost of traditional marriage in Nigeria.
body: What was supposed to be a beautiful celebration of love reportedly took an unexpected turn in Mbaise, Imo State, after a groom allegedly walked away from his bride and their traditional wedding arrangements.
## What reportedly happened
According to reports circulating online, trouble began when the bride's family demanded ₦1.2 million as bride price, a sum that reportedly did not sit well with the groom.
Rather than go ahead with the marriage under those conditions, the man allegedly called everything off, leaving the bride and both families in an embarrassing situation.
## The cost of getting married
The incident has raised fresh questions about the financial demands sometimes placed on intending couples during traditional marriage ceremonies.
Some people believe families have every right to uphold their marriage customs. Others argue that excessive financial demands can discourage young people who genuinely want to settle down.

The full circumstances of the reported incident, including whether the ₦1.2 million covered only the bride price or other traditional marriage expenses as well, have not been independently confirmed, and the people involved have not been identified.
## Over to you
Should a man walk away from a marriage because of expensive traditional demands, or should both families find a way to reach an agreement?
What would you do if you were in his shoes?
more: The incident reportedly happened in Mbaise, Imo State.
The bride's family allegedly asked for ₦1.2 million.

stories.h: Nathaniel Bassey becomes first African gospel singer to pass 1 billion YouTube views
stories.p: Gospel singer and pastor Nathaniel Bassey has reportedly become the first African gospel artist to pass one billion views on YouTube. The milestone came during this month's edition of his Hallelujah Challenge worship programme.
body: Nigerian gospel singer and pastor Nathaniel Bassey has reached a milestone no other African gospel artist has achieved, according to reports on Monday, 2 November 2026.
## The milestone

His main YouTube channel had passed 1.014 billion views at the time of reporting, with about 5.24 million subscribers. The channel has been active since 2011. Among his most popular songs are 'Imela', 'Onise Iyanu', 'Olowogbogboro' and 'You Are God', which are sung in churches across Nigeria and the diaspora.
## The Hallelujah Challenge

The milestone came during the October 2026 edition of the Hallelujah Challenge, the midnight prayer and worship programme Bassey started in 2017. It runs twice a year and draws huge online audiences, with many viewers joining live on Instagram and YouTube. Earlier this week, a plane crash survivor shared a testimony during the programme, and a Muslim woman's decision to join drew attention online.
## A non-commercial approach

Some of Bassey's followers have suggested he should make money from the large audience. He has previously described the Hallelujah Challenge as a spiritual exercise focused on devotion and worship rather than revenue. He did not give a public statement about the milestone at the time of reporting.
## Background

Bassey, who is also a trumpeter, has become one of the best-known voices in Nigerian worship music. His success shows the growing global reach of Nigerian gospel music, which has produced several international stars in recent years.
## How fans reacted
Fans celebrated the news online, describing it as a proud moment for African gospel music.
more: His channel has more than 1.01 billion views and 5.24 million subscribers.
The milestone came during the Hallelujah Challenge.

stories.h: Tinubu hosts governors, Ribadu and Gbajabiamila at dinner in Makkah
stories.p: President Tinubu hosted a dinner for members of his delegation in Makkah on Sunday, including the governors of Yobe, Kaduna, Jigawa, Sokoto and Borno, NSA Nuhu Ribadu and Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila. He prayed for Nigeria and urged citizens to see the country's diversity as a strength.
body: President Bola Tinubu has hosted senior government officials, state governors and business leaders at a dinner in Makkah, Saudi Arabia, during his Umrah pilgrimage.
## Who attended

According to a statement by the President's adviser on information and strategy, Bayo Onanuga, on Sunday, 1 November 2026, those at the dinner included Yobe Governor Mai Mala Buni, Kaduna Governor Uba Sani, Jigawa Governor Mohammed Namadi, Sokoto Governor Ahmed Aliyu and Borno Governor Babagana Zulum. Also present were National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu, Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila, Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate, political adviser Ibrahim Masari and Oando chief executive Wale Tinubu. Kwara Governor Abdulrahman AbdulRazaq, BUA chairman Abdul Samad Rabiu and Attorney-General Lateef Fagbemi also spoke at the event.
## What the President said

Tinubu reportedly prayed for peace, unity and prosperity in Nigeria and urged Nigerians to see the country's ethnic, religious and cultural diversity as a strength. He said Nigeria's people and natural resources provide a foundation for an inclusive and prosperous nation, and asked God to turn the country's diversity into prosperity. Guests offered prayers for the President and the country.
## Background

Tinubu travelled to Saudi Arabia on 29 October for the Umrah pilgrimage. The trip has been criticised by opposition figures, including Atiku Abubakar, who claimed it was a cover for travel to France, and activist Omoyele Sowore, who claimed it was for medical treatment. The Presidency has rejected both claims. It says the President is expected back in Nigeria this week.
## How people reacted
Supporters shared photos of the dinner as evidence of the President's good health, while critics questioned the cost of taking a large delegation abroad.
more: Five governors, Ribadu and Gbajabiamila were among the guests.
Tinubu urged Nigerians to see diversity as a strength.

stories.h: Seun Okinbaloye says his 2027 rigging warning named no party or candidate
stories.p: Channels TV anchor Seun Okinbaloye has clarified his widely shared warning about rigging in the 2027 elections, saying it did not accuse any party, candidate or sponsor. Reactions remain divided, with some praising his courage and others accusing him of backtracking.
body: Popular Channels Television anchor Seun Okinbaloye has responded to the storm over his recent comments on election rigging ahead of 2027.
## What he said

Speaking on the channel on Sunday, 1 November 2026, Okinbaloye said his earlier remarks had been widely misread. He said his warning had named no political party, accused no candidate and identified no sponsor. Critics had interpreted his original comments as a claim that rigging of the 2027 elections had already begun.
## Background

Okinbaloye's original warning went viral last week, coming amid wider concerns about the integrity of the voter register after INEC admitted that some of its registration officers had entered AI-generated photos. Opposition candidates, including Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, have called for audits and promised to prosecute anyone involved in rigging. INEC says the register is still being cleaned up and will be certified in December.
## How people reacted

Opinion was divided. Some viewers praised the anchor for speaking out and for clarifying his position, saying he was simply doing his job as a journalist. Others accused him of damage control and asked why he had not named those he believed were planning to rig. Several users said INEC itself should identify and prosecute staff involved in irregularities in the register.
## Why it matters

Okinbaloye presents one of Nigeria's most-watched political programmes, and his comments carry weight with voters and politicians alike. The debate shows how sensitive questions about election credibility have become as campaigning intensifies.
more: Okinbaloye says his warning named no party, candidate or sponsor.
He says his earlier comments were misread.
Reactions remain divided online.

stories.h: Yul Edochie shares date-night video with Judy Austin amid breakup rumours
stories.p: Yul Edochie has posted a cosy video with his second wife, Judy Austin, after weeks of quiet that led fans to speculate about a split. Judy also called him her 'baby for life', but some fans remain sceptical.
body: Nollywood actor Yul Edochie appears to have answered rumours about the state of his marriage to actress Judy Austin with a romantic video.
## What they posted

On Sunday, 1 November 2026, Yul shared an Instagram video of himself and Judy relaxing together on a night out, wishing fans a happy new month. Judy also shared footage from the date night, describing him as her partner for life. Neither addressed the rumours directly.
## The rumours

The couple had been unusually quiet on social media in recent weeks, which led some fans to speculate that they had split. Some even linked Yul to another actress after he attended her birthday party, claims that were never confirmed.
## How people reacted

Reactions were mixed. Some fans welcomed the video and said it put the rumours to rest, while others questioned whether the couple were truly happy and described the post as damage control. Yul also drew criticism this week for reposting a fan-made video about his life that included footage of his first wife, May Edochie.
## Background

Yul Edochie, the son of veteran actor Pete Edochie, announced in 2022 that he had taken Judy Austin as a second wife, sparking a long public dispute with May Edochie, his first wife. May later went to court over the marriage, and the matter has remained a talking point among Nollywood fans. Yul also defended polygamy this week in a discussion about a US pastor's second marriage.
more: Yul shared a cosy date-night video with Judy Austin.
Fans had speculated about a split after weeks of quiet.

stories.h: Havertz goal gives Arsenal first league win at Anfield in 14 years, sends them top
stories.p: Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 at Anfield on Sunday through Kai Havertz's early goal, moving to the top of the Premier League with 24 points. It was the Gunners' first league win at Anfield in 14 years.
body: Arsenal have moved to the top of the Premier League after ending a long wait for a league win at Anfield.
## The match

Kai Havertz scored the only goal in the 16th minute on Sunday, 1 November 2026, turning in a cross from Declan Rice at the back post. Liverpool controlled long spells of the game and pushed hard for an equaliser, with two penalty appeals turned down and Florian Wirtz hitting the crossbar from a free-kick. Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya denied Alexander Isak, while at the other end Alisson made a late save to stop substitute Christos Tzolis from doubling the lead.
## The table

The result takes Arsenal to 24 points, three ahead of Manchester City, who reportedly lost to Brighton on the same day. It was Arsenal's first league win at Anfield in 14 years, ending a run of 13 league visits without victory.
## What Arteta said

Manager Mikel Arteta told the BBC that the win was for everyone connected to the club and that 14 years without a victory at Anfield was a long time. He praised his players' performance but said it was too early to talk about the title race, adding that the team would now prepare for a big European match in Prague.
## Why it matters

Arsenal have finished as runners-up in recent seasons and are hoping to win their first league title since 2004. The win at one of the hardest grounds in English football will boost their belief, while Liverpool will be disappointed not to have taken anything from a game they dominated for long periods.
more: Havertz scored in the 16th minute from Rice's cross.
Arsenal are top with 24 points, three ahead of Manchester City.
It was their first league win at Anfield in 14 years.

stories.h: Yahaya Bello vows to spend two weeks in Kano campaigning for Tinubu
stories.p: Former Kogi governor Yahaya Bello has reportedly pledged to move to Kano for two weeks to campaign for President Tinubu and Governor Abba Yusuf. He urged non-indigenous communities in the state to deliver more votes than in 2023.
body: Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has promised to personally campaign in Kano for President Bola Tinubu's re-election.
## What he said

Speaking at a political mobilisation and empowerment programme for Yoruba and other non-indigenous communities in Kano, organised by the foundation of Rep. Leke Abejide and reported on Sunday, 1 November 2026, Bello said he would move to Kano for two weeks to campaign for the President and for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf. He urged non-indigenous communities in the state to beat the nearly 500,000 votes they reportedly gave Tinubu in 2023, and said Abejide's network could deliver at least two million votes. He also pointed to work on the Kano–Abuja highway as evidence of the President's commitment to the North.
## Support for communities

Abejide, who represents Yagba Federal Constituency in Kogi State and holds a Yoruba community title in Kano, announced ₦500 million in interest-free loans for women's cooperatives, along with support for widows. He said programmes for young people and men are being planned.
## Background

Kano has the second-highest number of registered voters in Nigeria after Lagos, and the APC is investing heavily there after Governor Yusuf moved from the NNPP to the APC. The state is also the home of Rabiu Kwankwaso, Peter Obi's running mate on the NDC ticket. Bello, who governed Kogi from 2016 to 2024, is facing a money-laundering case brought by the EFCC, which he denies. Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin also predicted a Tinubu victory at an APC event in Kano on Sunday.
## What happens next
The campaign in Kano is expected to intensify as the APC and NDC compete for the state's large vote.

stories.h: Atiku says Tinubu has broken his promise of constant electricity
stories.p: Atiku Abubakar's campaign has accused President Tinubu of failing to keep his 2022 promise to provide constant electricity within four years. The ADC candidate says settling power-sector debts and passing laws is not the same as delivering power, and pledged to replace the band tariff system.
body: The presidential campaign of Atiku Abubakar has accused President Bola Tinubu of breaking a key campaign promise on electricity.
## What Atiku's campaign said

In a statement issued on Sunday, 1 November 2026, by Phrank Shaibu, communications director of the ADC presidential campaign, the campaign recalled that Tinubu promised during his 2022 campaign that Nigerians should not vote for him again if he failed to provide constant electricity in four years. The statement accused the ruling APC of hiding the failure behind announcements of new laws, bonds and committees, saying that settling old debts owed to power companies is not the same as building new generation capacity. It argued that signing a law or raising a bond does not produce electricity.
## Tariffs and taxes

The campaign also questioned what would happen to electricity bills when subsidies end in 2027, although officials have said there will be no immediate tariff rise. It criticised a planned 5 per cent surcharge on some fuels under the Nigeria Tax Act, which the government says is not yet active. Atiku pledged to work with states and regulators to replace the current band system with a framework based on how much electricity customers actually receive.
## The government's position

The Federal Government says it is fixing the power sector step by step. This week the Federal Executive Council approved procurement for new East and West super grids to raise transmission capacity to 19,000MW within two years, and the Minister of Power set a long-term target of 70,000MW by 2060. The government has also paid part of the debts owed to gas suppliers and power companies. The APC had not responded to Atiku's latest statement at the time of the report.
## Why it matters
Electricity supply is one of the issues that matter most to voters, and all the main candidates have made promises on power.
more: Atiku says Tinubu has not delivered the constant power he promised in 2022.
He says paying debts and passing laws is not the same as generating power.
He promises to replace the band tariff system.

stories.h: VeryDarkMan brings out cash counting machine after claiming record ₦90 million sales in one day
stories.p: VeryDarkMan has brought out a cash counting machine to count money reportedly received from sales of his RATEL products, after saying the business made ₦90 million in a single day. He has also promised to make his bank statement public to clear any doubts.
body: Social media activist and businessman VeryDarkMan (VDM) has once again got people talking, this time after bringing out a cash counting machine to count money reportedly received from the sale of his RATEL products.
Photos show him and a colleague surrounded by bundles of naira notes, with an open suitcase full of cash, stacks of money on cartons of RATEL power stations and a counting machine beside them.
## A record day
According to VDM, the business recorded about ₦90 million in sales in one day, the biggest single-day figure since the products were launched.
## Ready to show proof
VDM knows how Nigerians think. Once you mention ₦90 million in one day, some people will immediately start asking questions, while others will simply refuse to believe it.

To clear the doubts, he has promised to go a step further and make his bank account statement public so people can see the transactions for themselves. He appeared confident about the figures and made it clear he was ready to back up his claims with evidence.
## A fast-growing brand

What makes this development interesting is how quickly the RATEL business appears to be gaining attention. From importing products from China to demonstrating how they perform in public, VDM has continued to attract customers and supporters.
However, the ₦90 million figure has yet to be independently verified, and sales revenue should not be confused with profit.
## Over to you
If VDM can truly generate ₦90 million in sales in a single day, imagine what this business could become in the next few years.
What do you think about the speed at which VeryDarkMan is growing the RATEL brand?
more: VDM says RATEL made about ₦90 million in sales in one day.
He has promised to publish his bank statement.
The figure has not been independently verified.

stories.h: Landlord seriously injured as dispute with tenant over rent increase from ₦300,000 to ₦1 million turns violent
stories.p: A disagreement between a Nigerian landlord and his tenant over renovation costs and a proposed rent increase from ₦300,000 to ₦1 million has reportedly ended in violence. The landlord was allegedly struck on the head and seriously injured.
body: A disagreement between a Nigerian landlord and his tenant over house renovation expenses and a proposed rent increase has reportedly ended in violence, leaving the landlord seriously injured.
## How it started

According to reports, trouble began when the landlord decided to raise the rent from ₦300,000 to a staggering ₦1 million. Renovation costs also became a major point of disagreement between both parties.
## The confrontation

What should have been a discussion about rent and property maintenance allegedly turned into a physical confrontation, during which the tenant reportedly struck the landlord on the head, causing serious injuries.

Photos circulating online show a man with plasters on his head and another man seated in what appears to be an office. The identities of those involved have not been confirmed, and the details of the incident have not been independently verified.
## Rising tension over rent
The incident has raised questions about the growing tension between landlords and tenants in Nigeria, at a time when many families are already struggling with the rising cost of accommodation.
Landlords have their own expenses to deal with, but tenants are equally feeling the pressure of sudden and substantial rent increases.
However serious a disagreement becomes, violence should never be the answer.
## Over to you

stories.h: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya introduces new wife as Fountain of Life Church welcomes another 'Mummy G.O.'
stories.p: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, has reportedly introduced his new wife to the congregation. The news has revived an old debate about how Nigerian churches treat divorce among their leaders compared with ordinary members.
body: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya, the Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, has reportedly introduced his new wife to the congregation, bringing fresh attention to his personal life and to the church's leadership.
Photos from the occasion show the couple dressed in matching red outfits, smiling together on the church stage.
## Background
For those who may not know, Pastor Jimmy was previously married to Kemi Odukoya, and the marriage produced two children. That marriage reportedly ended some years ago.

His sister, who also serves as an associate pastor in the church, has spoken publicly about the breakdown of her own marriage, including her personal experiences and how her faith in God carried her through that difficult period.
The Fountain of Life Church was founded by their late parents, Pastors Taiwo and Bimbo Odukoya, and the children have continued the family's ministry.
## A question about double standards
The news raises a question about how marriage and divorce are discussed in some Nigerian churches.

Many religious institutions regularly remind ordinary members that marriage is sacred and that the Bible says God hates divorce. Some believers are even made to feel guilty for leaving marriages that have become unbearable.

Yet when divorce happens within prominent pastoral families, the conversation often becomes more understanding. Suddenly, people are encouraged to consider personal circumstances, healing, forgiveness and new beginnings.
Perhaps they should. Pastors are human beings too. But shouldn't ordinary church members receive that same understanding?
## Finding love again

There is nothing wrong with anyone finding love again after a failed marriage. The concern is the apparent gap between what some churches preach to their members and how they respond when their own leaders face similar situations.
So the question is this: if divorce can be understood and accepted when it involves church leaders, why should ordinary Christians sometimes be made to feel condemned for the same decision?
What is your opinion?
more: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya was previously married to Kemi Odukoya.
The church was founded by his late parents, Taiwo and Bimbo Odukoya.
The news has reopened debate about how churches handle divorce.
